historical_references.reference: The Battle of Novara (1513) was a significant military engagement between the French and the Holy Roman Empire during the Italian Wars. It marked the end of Louis XII of France's bid for Italian hegemony and enabled the Holy Roman Emperor, Maximilian I, to assert his control over northern Italy. The battle took place near the city of Novara in Lombardy.

Novara became the site of a major military confrontation during the First Italian War (1848-1849), when the Sardinian army, led by King Carlo Alberto, defeated the Austrian army, led by Field Marshal Radetzky. The battle marked the end of Austrian dominance in northern Italy and paved the way for the unification of Italy under the House of Savoy.
